decisions.reason: Changing the proposal's brand identity does not alter the requirement to integrate photos into the final proposal draft.
The document layout, pass count, input stage, and coverage remain unchanged; brand identity is owned by the source Requirement.
The switch to Agua Arc branding does not change the requirement to include and format supplied tables in the final draft.
The required print-ready PDF delivery format remains valid regardless of the proposal's brand identity.
The branding change does not alter Canva source access, editability, or ownership; those matters are addressed separately in the same message.
Packaging the RFQ response content into one document remains required and is not changed by replacing client branding with bidder branding.
The Agua Arc branding decision does not change the established count of one consolidated revision round.
The branding clause does not change the delivery schedule; the same message's turnaround changes are already represented by a separate candidate Event.
The anticipated RFQ page count remains unchanged by the proposal branding decision.
The source decision concerns the separate GreenLatinos RFQ proposal and Agua Arc identity, not the TPEC proposal.
